# std.ops

The traits that give `==`, `<`, `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`, `-a`, `^`, `|`, `&`, `in` and `by` their meaning (R08.1.5), `T.zero` and `T.one`, and the numbers' own impls of them. Core re-exports them, so no module imports them.

In prelude (no `use` needed): `Bounded`.

## `trait Eq`

`a == b` and `a != b` (R08.1.5).

## `trait Ord(Eq)`

`a < b`, and from it `>`, `<=` and `>=` (R08.1.5).

## `trait Add<Rhs = Self>`

`a + b` on a type that is not a number (R08.1.5); `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`, `**` and `-a` likewise.

## `trait Sub<Rhs = Self>`

## `trait Mul<Rhs = Self>`

## `trait Div<Rhs = Self>`

## `trait Rem<Rhs = Self>`

## `trait Pow<Rhs = Int>`

`a ** e`: `a` to the power `e`, an `Int` unless the impl says otherwise.

## `trait Neg`

## `trait BitXor<Rhs = Self>`

## `trait BitOr<Rhs = Self>`

## `trait BitAnd<Rhs = Self>`

## `trait Contains<T>`

`x in s`: whether `s` holds `x`, sub-linear; `x not in s` is its negation (R12.4.7).

## `trait By<Rhs = Int>`

`w by k`: every `k`-th value of a walk that is not a range literal, from its first, as a walk of the same type (R01.8.4); `(0..10).rev by 3` is `9, 6, 3, 0`.

## `trait Zero`

The numbers' own operators, so `T: Add` holds of them.

## `trait One`

`T.one`: the identity of `T`'s `*`, where a product starts.

## `trait Bounded`

`T.MIN`, `T.MAX`: the least and greatest values of `T`, so `max` and `min` over it have an identity (R02.2.1, decision 580).

## `trait Alike<T>`

A tuple whose fields are all `T`: what `max` and `min` take past their first two values.

## Functions

- `fn max<T: Ord, Ts: Alike<T>>(a: T, b: T, ..more: Ts) -> T` — The largest of two or more values, the first of equal ones (R11.3.3).
- `fn min<T: Ord, Ts: Alike<T>>(a: T, b: T, ..more: Ts) -> T` — The smallest of two or more values, the first of equal ones (R11.3.3).
